text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Sporting soccer club president Jose Roquette is confident about the financial future of the club.
- Lisbon's Expo 1998 world fair may not bring profits, Prime Minister Antonio Guterres told parliament yesterday.

- The European Commission has doubts about the legality of the guarantee which the Portuguese state gave in the award of a 30 billion escudos loan to cereals company EPAC. The Commission seeks explanations from the Government.
- The Champalimaud group is to launch a bid for Banco Totta & Acores (BTA) in order to integrate it with Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor.
- Jose Torres Campos, who now heads state motorway company Brisa, was appointed chief organiser of Lisbon's Expo 98 world fair after the surprise resignation of Antonio Cardoso e Cunha.
- Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI) estimates the value of energy company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal at 1,300 billion escudos.
- Spanish bank Santander bought, through participating companies, five billion escudos of bad debt of Banco de Comercio e Industria, BCI president Costa Pinto told the paper.
- Fertiliser company Quimigal Adubos posted about 1.5 billion escudos profits in 1996, 90 pct more than in 1995, Quimigal president Luis Pereira Filipe said.
